originalTitle: Ahead of Market: 10 things that will decide stock market action on Friday
simplifiedContent: The Indian stock market didn't do very well because of worries about what's happening in the world, even though some companies are expected to report good earnings. On Friday, the market might be affected by how individual companies perform, especially those in finance, cars, and technology. The Nifty, which is a measure of the market's overall performance, is expected to stay within a certain range because investors are being cautious. This means that the market might not go up or down too much, and investors will be watching specific companies to see how they do. The market's performance on Friday will depend on these factors, and investors will be waiting to see what happens.

originalTitle: AI trade moves from chips to electricity: Why 7 power stocks are gaining Wall Street attention with gains up to 86%
simplifiedContent: Here's a simple explanation of the news: Some big investors on Wall Street are paying attention to companies that make electricity because they think these companies will do well due to the growing need for power to run computers and data centers used for artificial intelligence (AI). This is a change from their previous focus on companies that make computer chips. As a result, the stock prices of some of these electricity-related companies have risen by as much as 86%. These companies include those that produce nuclear power, build grid infrastructure, and make cooling systems. This shift in investor interest matters because it could be a good opportunity for other investors to consider putting their money into these types of companies.

originalTitle: Market Trading Guide: ABB India among 2 stock recommendations for Friday
simplifiedContent: Here's a simple explanation of the news: The Indian stock market had a slow day due to worries about global politics and fluctuating oil prices. Despite this, analysts suggest buying two specific stocks: Chennai Petroleum and ABB India. They think these stocks will do well because their prices have recently broken through important levels, and many people are buying them, which could mean they will continue to rise. This is also because their prices are higher than their average prices over time, which is a good sign. Overall, analysts think these stocks have a good chance of going up in value.

originalTitle: Caliber Mining IPO raises  ₹135 crore from anchor investors ahead of issue opening
simplifiedContent: Caliber Mining and Logistics Limited is raising money by selling shares to the public, and before the public sale starts, they sold some shares to big investors. These big investors, including some mutual funds, bought 31,83,961 shares at a price of ₹424 each, giving the company ₹134.99 crore. This sale happened before the main public sale, which is set to start on July 17, 2026. This matter because it shows that big investors are interested in buying shares of Caliber Mining, which could be a good sign for the company's stock. The company is able to raise a significant amount of money, ₹134.99 crore, which will likely be used to help the business grow.

originalTitle: SBI Funds Management IPO closes with 42x subscription, led by strong QIB demand; GMP signals healthy listing
simplifiedContent: SBI Funds Management's initial public offering (IPO) got a very strong response from investors, with 42 times more bids than available shares. This means that the company received bids for 519 crore shares, which is much more than they were offering. The price of the shares was set between ₹545 and ₹575, but due to high demand, the expected listing price is ₹669, which is 16.55% higher than the top end of the price range. This strong demand and expected high listing price are good signs for the company's stock market debut. The high demand, especially from big institutional investors, suggests that the company's stock may do well when it starts trading.

originalTitle: Alpine Texworld IPO sails through on Day 3: Check subscription status, GMP and other key details
simplifiedContent: Alpine Texworld's initial public offering (IPO) was successful, with more people wanting to buy shares than were available. The company wanted to raise 126 crore rupees to build a new weaving unit in Ahmedabad, and they were able to do so. The IPO was subscribed 1.4 times, which means that for every share available, 1.4 people wanted to buy it. The company will now give out the shares to investors on July 17, and the shares will start trading on the stock market on July 21. This is important because it shows that investors are interested in the company and its plans for the future.
